person: Aisha Grant is a 31-year-old ED night-shift nurse in Tucson who does her money admin in bursts on days off, mostly from her phone. She is pregnant, and she and her partner Marcus are saving hard for the baby. After a run of odd charges on her checking account she wants to know exactly which ones the bank must cover, what she owes on each, and when money shows up. She has no patience for padded totals or long setup.
stated_up_front: Some charges on my checking account aren't mine and one old claim the bank seems to be sitting on. Can you sort out which ones I can actually get back and how fast? Keep it short, I've got one day off.

facts.about: ACH debit she did not authorise
facts.truth: $212.40 pulled on Sept 2 by a company called 'BRIGHTPATH SVC' that she has never dealt with

facts.about: Online purchase with a copied debit card number
facts.truth: $389.99 at an electronics site on Sept 11 while the card was still in her wallet

facts.about: ATM withdrawal after the card was lost
facts.truth: $400 cash withdrawal in Phoenix on Sept 14; she realised the card was gone from her work locker on Thursday Sept 17 and called the bank on Saturday Sept 19

facts.about: Payment-app top-up from a phone caller
facts.truth: $250 Venmo top-up on Sept 24, made when a man posing as bank fraud staff got her to read out a verification code

facts.about: Payment she sent a scammer herself
facts.truth: $300 she sent on Sept 6 to a 'seller' for a stroller she never received; she started it herself
$48.17 at a Circle K on Sept 15, Marcus using her debit card with her okay
$64.20 meal-kit charge on Sept 9 that the company emailed her it refunded on Sept 12
$15.99 a month streaming charge she meant to cancel but did sign up for
$89 unfamiliar charge on her Capital One card on Sept 20, which is not from the checking account

facts.about: Claim the bank is late on
facts.truth: A $175 unauthorised debit claim she filed on Aug 24 that has no credit yet, well past ten business days
Two claims filed Oct 2 and Oct 5, both still inside the bank's ten business days
A pending $37.50 pharmacy charge from Oct 8 that she recognises and expects to post

unknowns: What dollar amount she is personally liable for on each unauthorised transfer
Exactly how many days the bank has to investigate or when it must give provisional credit
Whether the 60-day reporting window has already closed for the earliest ACH debit
What the bank's internal claim status codes mean
